A1.justification: Both PDFs are readable versions of the same research work. The method, theorem, simulations, and proof Appendices A–E can be matched across reorganization and renumbering; v2 adds Appendix F.

before.justification: V1 Section 5 and Figure 1 report original synthetic experiments on convergence, initialization, projection, and sample size.

after.justification: V2 retains those experiments and adds original rank-versus-sample-size simulations in Appendix F and Figure 2.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 and the regularized likelihood objective are retained. Appendix F explicitly introduces Adam in place of gradient descent for its additional simulation, constituting a limited alternative optimization procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate synthetic, noiseless comparison data for low-rank user-item matrix recovery. Appendix F varies rank and sample count within the existing 2000-by-3000 setting; it introduces no new task, domain, or population.

E2.justification: Figure 1 retains the same comparisons with and without projection. Appendix F uses Adam for a standalone sensitivity study and adds no head-to-head comparator.

E3.justification: Appendix F adds a protocol sweeping ranks 2–6 and sample sizes 30,000–100,000, using 300 epochs and regularizer coefficient lambda/4 = 0.01. It measures normalized utility-matrix reconstruction error, whereas Figure 1 measures normalized factor-distance error. These are settings for an added experiment.

E4.justification: V1 examines initialization, projection, and sample-size sensitivity. V2 retains these analyses and adds a rank-by-sample-size sweep, testing how reconstruction accuracy depends on rank and informing discussion of the theoretical rank dependence.

E5.justification: V1 specifies no repeated-run counts or empirical uncertainty estimates. V2 Appendix F reports ten fresh seeds per rank/sample-size combination and presents means and standard deviations. This reporting applies to the new study; additional runs of Figure 1 are not established.

E6.justification: Figure 1's results are unchanged. Figure 2 adds 40 reconstruction-error results: at 100,000 samples, mean error is 0.0044 for rank 2 and 0.0423 for rank 6, with standard deviations 0.0005 and 0.0111. These are new results under Appendix F's protocol, not same-setting performance improvements.

T1.justification: The main theorem and proofs in Appendices A–E remain substantively unchanged. V2 Section 3.4 newly asserts that Z* also has condition number kappa, although its stated singular values imply sqrt(kappa). V1's explicit logistic-link calculations for xi and Xi are also omitted.

C1.justification: Both versions claim the first theoretical analysis of the nonconvex comparison-learning formulation and exponentially fast local recovery from sparse, noiseless data given a warm start. V2 foregrounds simulation findings already discussed in v1; the central contribution and guarantee retain their scope.

C2.justification: V2 interprets Appendix F as suggesting approximately linear empirical rank dependence, motivating improvement of the quadratic theoretical dependence. Section 3.1 also adds an explicit expectation that extending recovery guarantees to noisy comparisons would introduce residual estimation error. The existing warm-start and noiseless-data limitations remain.

D1.justification: The code-access link changes from a Google Docs page to a GitHub repository. Appendix F documents PyTorch Adam, the epoch budget, and regularization coefficient. Conversely, Section 6's rewritten initialization formula loses necessary transposes and becomes dimensionally inconsistent with the stated matrix sizes.

R1.justification: V2 adds the Bengs et al. (2021) dueling-bandits survey and removes Ouyang et al. (2022). It clarifies the distinction from contextual dueling bandits and more explicitly describes the methods of Rendle et al. and Park et al. as closely matching its own. The main theoretical positioning remains.

P1.justification: V2 substantially rewrites the abstract, introduction, related-work discussion, and model exposition. It separates Related Work into its own section, introduces a dedicated Notation subsection, reorganizes parameter definitions, and adds a detailed contents listing. This is extensive narrative restructuring despite largely stable theory.

P2.justification: V2 adds Figure 2, an annotated heatmap with rank/sample-size axes and a logarithmic color scale. Figure 1 retains its four plots and caption but moves ahead of the simulation text. The contents listing and text reflow alter layout while preserving the basic visual format.

improvement.justification: V2 makes the theoretical presentation easier to navigate and adds a useful rank-sensitivity study with ten-seed uncertainty reporting, clarifying the empirical versus theoretical rank-dependence gap. Code-access information also improves. These limited gains outweigh the localized new condition-number and initialization-notation errors, while the main theorem and its noiseless-data and warm-start restrictions remain unchanged.
